note: Owner rulings applied on top of the immutable Pass 1 authority. The Pass 1 file is never edited; the working Pass 2 authority is derived by tools/build-feat-tags-pass2-semantic-authority.mjs. Tag operations are asserted against the Pass 1 tag sets (an ADD of a present tag or a REMOVE of an absent tag fails the build). Batch 1 final closeout adds two family-level terminal rulings (Martial Arts tier family; Grapple residual evidence) with no tag mutation.

tagChanges.name: Great Cleave
tagChanges.reason: Great Cleave explicitly uses the Cleave mechanic with the per-round limit removed. Cleave's drop-an-enemy trigger/setup remains part of the mechanic.

tagChanges.name: Pin
tagChanges.reason: A grapple attack is treated as an unarmed attack under the Core rules, and Pin prevents the target from moving or taking actions.

tagChanges.name: Crush
tagChanges.reason: Crush operates on a successful Pin/grapple and deals unarmed/claw damage. The Pin interaction is explicit in the Benefit, not prerequisite inference.

tagChanges.name: Throw
tagChanges.reason: Throw uses a grapple attack, forcibly relocates the target, leaves it prone, deals unarmed-equivalent damage, and ends the grapple. It does not pin or maintain restraint.

tagChanges.name: Trip
tagChanges.reason: Trip is executed through a grapple attack, which Core explicitly treats as an unarmed attack.

tagChanges.name: Martial Arts I
tagChanges.reason: The certified canonical content authority explicitly records the Core combat-rule interaction that Martial Arts I allows an unarmed character to threaten and make attacks of opportunity. Not propagated to Martial Arts II or III from prerequisites; each feat is adjudicated on its own rules.

tagChanges.name: Cut the Red Tape
tagChanges.reason: The feat explicitly preserves entitlement to Gather Information rerolls when making the substituted Knowledge (bureaucracy) check.

tagChanges.name: Informer
tagChanges.reason: Informer explicitly carries eligible Gather Information rerolls onto the substituted Perception check; aligned with the reroll-inheritance treatment used elsewhere in the shared ontology.

tagChanges.name: Gunnery Specialist
tagChanges.reason: Not prerequisite leakage. The Special clause changes the Starship Tactics maneuvers available through this feat based on whether the character is trained in Pilot, so the skill mechanically participates in the feat.

tagChanges.name: Slammer
tagChanges.reason: The persistent condition caused by Slammer can be removed by a DC 20 Treat Injury check; under the owner skill-completeness rule that is a direct mechanical interaction with Treat Injury. Slammer imposes the condition; it does not itself perform medical recovery.

rejectedFindings.name: Vehicular Surge
rejectedFindings.reason: Pilot is a prerequisite. "Vehicle you pilot" describes character role, not use or modification of the Pilot skill.

rejectedFindings.name: Mounted Defense
rejectedFindings.reason: The Benefit works while riding a beast or speeder bike as passenger or pilot. Pilot appears only as an alternative prerequisite.

rejectedFindings.name: Mission Specialist
rejectedFindings.reason: Generic choose-one-trained-skill feat, correctly represented by `skills`. The Use the Force sentence is an eligibility exception for one possible choice, not Force-specialized semantics.

rejectedFindings.name: Logic Upgrade: Skill Swap
rejectedFindings.reason: Use the Force is explicitly excluded from selectable skills. An exclusion does not create positive Use the Force semantics.

rejectedFindings.name: Flurry
rejectedFindings.reason: Flurry substitutes for a feat when qualifying for a prestige class, not one skill for another.

rejectedFindings.name: Weapon Finesse
rejectedFindings.reason: Weapon Finesse substitutes Dexterity for Strength on attack rolls, not a skill.

rejectedFindings.name: Droid Shield Mastery
rejectedFindings.reason: Changes Endurance success/action timing, not skill identity; it already carries `endurance`.

familyReviews.label: Power Attack / Powerful Charge / Bantha Rush
familyReviews.reason: The common `melee` relationship is real, but the differing tags represent differing mechanics: Power Attack is an attack-for-damage trade; Powerful Charge is movement/charge plus attack/damage enhancement; Bantha Rush is forced movement/control. Tag parity is not forced.

familyReviews.label: Ranged precision family
familyReviews.reason: `ranged` + `precision` is the valid common core. Aim, cover, positioning, range-band, sniper, setup, targeting, and damage tags remain mechanic-specific.

familyReviews.label: Tech Specialist family
familyReviews.reason: The valid common core is tech + mechanics + modification + equipment. The wider object/trait tags on Tech Specialist and Superior Tech are justified by their modification tables; Signature Device's `reliability` is justified by its take-10 mechanic; Hasty Modification does not inherit the parent feat's entire semantic payload.

familyReviews.label: martial-arts
familyReviews.reason: Martial Arts I alone records the Core cross-rule interaction that lets an otherwise unarmed character threaten and make attacks of opportunity. Martial Arts II and III independently advance unarmed damage and dodge Reflex Defense only. Prerequisite inheritance is not semantic inheritance; attack_of_opportunity is not propagated to II or III.

familyReviews.label: Grapple family (Pin / Crush / Throw / Trip)
familyReviews.reason: Remaining tag-set differences are mechanically justified: Pin restrains and prevents actions/movement; Crush deals damage through an established Pin; Throw forcibly relocates the target, knocks it prone and ends the grapple; Trip knocks the target prone. The Batch 1 corrections already set the common grapple/unarmed/melee semantics; tag parity is not forced. Member-level Batch 1 rulings (approved/corrected) remain recorded on the feat records.

invalidFamilyReferences.label: Rapid Shot / Improved Rapid Shot
invalidFamilyReferences.reason: There is no canonical Improved Rapid Shot identity in the 353-feat authority. The owner-named family reference was erroneous; no identity is invented. Rapid Strike / Improved Rapid Strike remains the valid canonical family.

publicationCategory.note: Publication category is structural metadata, not semantic evidence.
